Each round you will play a hen card from your hand, trying to create a harmonious barnyard with different hen breeds. The rules to place cards are a few and simple, but the difficulty will be on making large groups of hens of the same breed. At the end of the game you will gain points from your largest group of hens of the same breed in your barnyard, from your rooster token and from the goal card. Don’t forget some rare hens give you medals worth points at the end of the game. The hens breeder with the best barnyard wins! Number of players: 1 - 4 Game duration: 13 mn Complexity: 3 / 5 Play Hens and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. With your friends and thousands of players from the whole world. Free. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Rooster 4 Cards in the Deck 5 Game End Overview You are trying to have the most of the same Hen type by game's end Turn On your turn you will draw 2 new cards, play one card, discard one card For each card drawn, you can either draw from the deck or from an opponent's discard pile (you cannot draw from an opponent in the first round) Place a hen in your 4x3 or 3x4 grid whilst respecting orthogonal adjacency rules, the adjacent hens can either be the same breed (colour) and any number OR different breed/colour but 1 higher or lower in value (e.g. a 3 can go next to a 2 or a 4) If you cannot, or don't wish to, place a hen following placement rules, place it face down as a coop for -1 points but still adjacent to previously laid cards. After which, any hen can be placed adjacent to a coop, but still respecting any other adjacent hens. Finally, discard a hen from your hand Rooster At the end of the 6th round, all players simultaneously place their rooster token on a hen The group of hens marked by the rooster will score at the end in addition to the largest group unless they are the same, as such it's advised to NOT place the rooster on the group you think will be the largest Cards in the Deck There are 72 cards in the deck. The grid chart on the game board shows what cards exist and with what qualities (card number, eggs, medals). The red squares on this matrix show which cards have two copies. Game End The game ends at the end of the 12th round Count the eggs depicted on the largest continuous group of hens of the same breed (colour). If two or more groups tie for largest group, the group with the most eggs will score only Score points for the eggs of the contiguous group of hens in which rooster is placed, as long as it is not placed on the largest group of hens. In this case points will be scored only for this group, even if it contains fewer eggs than a group with the same number of Hen cards. For both types, eggs = 1vp each Any medals anywhere are added up and score 2 vp per 3 medals Each Coop is worth -1vp (negative) Score the two goals on the goal card, EVERYONE can score these if they apply, and note that some goals give negative points After which, the player with the most points wins! If tied, the player with the largest group of hens wins! If still tied, the player with the second largest group wins! If still tied, the player with the most medals wins! If still tied, the tied players both win! community_text:
[Rating: 3/10] The rule, that the adjacent cards with different colors must be EXACTLY 1 value higher/lower, and can't be equal is the most unnecessary and pointless rule I've ever heard.

[Rating: 3/10] Boring set collection based on constant boring accounting, random with minimum interaction. Not bad but I don’t want to play it again (3).

[Rating: 3/10] ok art but other than that it is a set collection kind of game with nothing that makes it outstanding. I would choose other set collection games.

[Rating: 3/10] After 2 games on BGA: A grid-based set collection that is mediocre in every respect. The artwork: mediocre. The variety of scoring options: mediocre. The feeling when you get penalized because you simply can’t play a matching card: mediocre. I would always prefer similar games like Pixies, Castle Combo, or "Ecosystem: Savanna".

[Rating: 4/10] (Played at 2p; likely better with more)  It's a lighter version of Arboretum and all the better for it. I like the snappier speed and simplified scoring. This is closer to feeling like Lost Cities for me. Not amazing but decent.  EDIT: Less good on the return play.

[Rating: 4/10] For such a small and somewhat inconsequential card game, I found the placement rules to be unnecessarily complicated and overly unintuitive.  Furthermore, the scoring with the medals and the rooster felt superfluous.  There is also a seemingly rare disadvantage to being the first player, I can say with confidence that I am not a fan.

[Rating: 4.5/10] It seems like a neat little card game. It also has a spatial part to it. Nothing that would ever be a favorite but friendly theme for the family. The scoring may take a moment for someone to understand. I think would be better in person rather than BGA.

[Rating: 5/10] Game is not bad and has some interesting ideas, but Arboretum is still better. Cards ergonomics could have been a lot better by just putting eggs/medals to sides.
